finding: Sebaceous (gland) carcinoma of the eyelid on histopathology — lobules of atypical cells with foamy lipid-laden vacuolated cytoplasm and pagetoid intraepithelial spread; it characteristically presents as unilateral chronic blepharoconjunctivitis or a recurrent chalazion

links.shows: Case with clinical and histopathologic images; the lesion mimicked chalazion and blepharoconjunctivitis, with atypical Meibomian glands on wedge biopsy

notes: The distractors map to other tumours: pearly ulcer with raised edges = basal cell carcinoma, nodule in sun-exposed skin = squamous cell carcinoma, pigmented caruncular lesion = melanocytic. Only sebaceous carcinoma gives chronic blepharoconjunctivitis.
